data.short_meaning: My father is a lamp; father of light
data.long_meaning: Abner (אַבְנֵר) is a name of Hebrew origin meaning “My father is a lamp; father of light”. A compound of Hebrew אָב ('av) 'father' (with the possessive yod) and נֵר (ner) 'lamp, light' - 'my father is a lamp' / 'father of light'. Its root is Hebrew אַבְנֵר (ʾAvner), from אָב ('av) 'father' + נֵר (ner) 'lamp, light'. Abner is the anglicised form of Biblical Hebrew ʾAvner.

faq.q: Does Abner appear in the Bible?
faq.a: Yes. The personal name occurs in the Hebrew Bible (1 Samuel 14:50; 2 Samuel 3).

faq.q: Is the meaning of Abner verified?
faq.a: The meaning “My father is a lamp; father of light” is supported by Old Testament: Abner, commander of King Saul's army (1 Samuel 14:50). Confidence: HIGH.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Abner?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abner total 40, reducing to 4. Number 4 is traditionally associated with stability, order and hard work. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Avner, Abner.

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Abner?
faq.a: Abner is transliterated as ʾAvner.

faq.q: How many syllables does Abner have?
faq.a: Abner has 2 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Abner?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Abner is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “My father is a lamp; father of light”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Abner used today?
faq.a: Abner circulates chiefly in Biblical Hebrew, English, Greek, Latin naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
